extracted.intended_audience: judge advocates, military lawyers, military administrators, and officials interpreting Army regulations and appropriation law
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal principles governing absence (with and without leave), furloughs, forfeiture of pay, and the scope/interpretation of appropriations for Army purposes. Intended to help military legal officers and administrators determine rights, liabilities, and allowable expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excusing delay in reporting after furlough due to government delay
rubrics_metrics.description: When a soldier on furlough applied for transportation in sufficient time to report on or before the last day of furlough but, due to delay of the Government, transportation was not furnished promptly and he did not report until after his furlough expired, the period between the last day of furlough and the date of actual reporting should be excused by proper authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the delay is excused the soldier would not forfeit the commutation of rations due. (Citations: G. 3988, 4758, 7211, 20203.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay in reporting may not be excused after discharge
rubrics_metrics.description: A delay in reporting at the expiration of a soldier's furlough may not be excused after the soldier has been discharged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furlough time and retirement service computation
rubrics_metrics.description: Time spent by an enlisted man on furlough should not be deducted in computing the 30 years' service necessary for retirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No double-counting of furlough absence for overseas enlistments
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier serving an enlistment in possessions beyond the seas cannot count absence on furlough double for the purpose of retirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite furloughs not to enable accepting commissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Furloughs for an indefinitely long period may not be granted to enlisted men so they may, during such furloughed period, accept commissions as officers of Philippine Scouts and serve as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation on commercial liner chargeable to soldier
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an enlisted man on furlough in the United States from an overseas possession was given an order for transportation on a commercial liner, such transportation is a proper charge against the soldier's pay and not properly at Government expense under the post commander's order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nurses appointed under Feb. 2, 1901 act are Army component and leaves not cumulative
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 19 of the act of Feb. 2, 1901 provides nurses may be granted leaves of absence for thirty days with pay each calendar year. Nurses appointed under the act are part of the United States Army (not civilian employees under contract) and may not be granted cumulative leaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conviction by civil courts while in civil custody constitutes absence without leave
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer of the Army in the hands of civil authorities who is convicted by civil courts is absent without leave; disposition of an appeal should be awaited to determine whether the absence is excused or unavoidable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to excuse absence vests in leave-granting officer and upward
rubrics_metrics.description: Under statute requiring that an officer absent without leave shall forfeit pay unless the absence be excused as unavoidable, the power to decide whether an absence in excess of granted leave is excused vests in the officer empowered by regulations to grant leaves; if beyond that commander's power, the power to excuse passes to the next higher commander and their conclusions are final unless appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an incident of leave-granting authority; the discretion created by statute must be exercised by the appropriate commander. (II A 2; C. 20764.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldier must endeavor to return; failure may ripen into desertion
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles of war require a soldier, when absent without authority, to endeavor constantly to return to duty; absence without such endeavor may, by lapse of time, establish animus non revertendi and ripen into desertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence from quarters only not within Article XXXII (desertion)
rubrics_metrics.description: An unauthorized absence from the quarters only (for example, after 11 p.m. inspection) is not properly chargeable under the 32d Article; that article contemplates absence from the troop, battery, company, or detachment (i.e., absence from the post or command).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital treatment elsewhere does not interrupt AWOL status
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier who absented himself without leave and, instead of reporting to his company, went elsewhere for medical care remains in the status of absence without leave; that status continues until muster-out of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrest by civil authorities during leave — duress and convictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a soldier absent with leave is arrested, tried, and convicted by civil authorities and fails to report at expiration of furlough, he becomes AWOL from that date. If held but not convicted, the holding should be regarded as duress; if convicted, the duress is due to the soldier's fault.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turnover to civil authorities on proper process suspends AWOL prosecution for that period
rubrics_metrics.description: When a soldier is turned over to civil authorities on service of proper process, prosecution will not lie for absence without leave during the time he is away being tried or serving sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability preventing return does not change AWOL status
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer or soldier while absent without leave who incurs a disability preventing return to duty does not have his status changed by that disability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting to quartermaster for transport does not terminate AWOL status
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier absent without leave who reports to a quartermaster for transportation back to his post does not, by such report, change his status as an absentee without leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper station for return transportation is where company/detachment serves
rubrics_metrics.description: Where expense is incurred transporting a soldier absent without authority to his proper station, the proper station is that at which his company or detachment is serving. The War Department may change the station, in which case the new assignment is the proper station within regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return placed on full duty without prosecution may be pleaded in defense
rubrics_metrics.description: If an officer or soldier on return from unauthorized absence reports the facts and is not proceeded against but is placed upon full duty by his commander, such action, under general custom, may be pleaded as a good defense if subsequently tried for the unauthorized absence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture of pay and allowances during AWOL accrues by operation of law
rubrics_metrics.description: An enlisted man forfeits his pay and allowances during the period of an absence without leave as provided in Army Regulations; during such absence he renders no service and therefore earns neither pay nor allowances. The forfeiture accrues independently of the result of a trial for the military offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Muster and pay rolls must show that he rendered no service; for absence of less than a day, sentence can impose forfeiture but such absence should not be noted on the rolls. Pay forfeited should cover the entire period of absence. (C. 12168; P. 36,303 Nov. 1889; P. 47,399 June 1891; C. 12577; C.12967; others.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquittal of military offense does not absolve payroll effects of absence
rubrics_metrics.description: If a soldier is tried for desertion and acquitted (not convicted of AWOL), his military record as to criminal offense may be clean, but the muster/pay rolls should still show failure to earn pay caused by absence without authority — a breach of contract which the rolls should reflect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make-good time rules under May 11, 1908 act
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the act of May 11, 1908, an enlisted man who absented himself without leave in an enlistment entered into after that act's approval must make good time so lost; for enlistments prior to the act he cannot be required to make good such absence except as provided in the 48th Article of War, though the period will not be regarded in computation of continuous service under the act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convicted and confined by civil authorities: AWOL but not required to make time good
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier arrested, tried, convicted, and held to serve sentence of civil authorities is absent without leave but cannot be held to make the time good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nunc pro tunc leave orders do not retroactively change AWOL status
rubrics_metrics.description: A nunc pro tunc order purporting to grant an officer a leave of absence for an overstayed period does not change his AWOL status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation for 'construction' includes all necessary expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: An appropriation for 'construction' of a telegraph line (or similar) includes all expenditures necessary to carry out the provisions of the act — e.g., mileage of officer to supervise, transportation of enlisted men, materials, hire of labor, erection of shelter, purchase of instruments, and every other expenditure necessary to carry out the act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative holding applying the general rule that expenditures legitimately incidental to the object of the appropriation are payable out of that appropriation. (51 R. 666, Mar. 12, 1887.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation does not cover items named in estimates unless act names or designates class
rubrics_metrics.description: An appropriation act does not include an article merely because it was named in the department estimates unless the appropriation act either names that article or designates a class of objects that would fairly and reasonably embrace that article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates may be used in construction, but an appropriation cannot be construed to appropriate for a specific estimated item unless the act names it or indicates the class. (54 F. 112, June 14, 1892.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations conforming to estimates imply authority to purchase articles named
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriations made in conformity with and based upon department estimates imply an authority to expend the appropriated funds for the articles designated in the estimates and imply legislative sanction of the objects for which the appropriations were asked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited holdings applying this executive-department practice. (51 R. 666; 41 F. 105; C.584.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual appropriations availability period (two-year rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An annual appropriation is available for two years after the expiration of the fiscal year (general rule noted in synopsis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the synopsis of appropriation law principles addressing period for which appropriations are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donated money cannot be expended until appropriated
rubrics_metrics.description: Money donated to the United States cannot be expended until Congress appropriates it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General principle summarized in appropriations synopsis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary contract expenses chargeable to appropriation even if incurred earlier
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary expenses required in preparation of a contract that is payable from an annual appropriation may be paid even though incurred before the beginning of the fiscal year for which the appropriation is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative application in synopsis: preliminary expenses preliminary to purchases for which an appropriation is made are chargeable to that appropriation. (See pages cited in synopsis.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Entire appropriation cannot be expended for partial performance only
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an appropriation is made for a certain object, the entire appropriation cannot be expended for partial performance only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General constraint on the use of appropriated funds (synopsis note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific appropriation cannot be supplemented by a general appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific appropriation cannot be supplemented by a general appropriation; funds appropriated for specific purposes are not augmented by unrelated general appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as an instances/axiom in appropriations synopsis.

rubrics_metrics.name: General words following enumeration are limited to like articles
rubrics_metrics.description: General words following the enumeration of special articles or classes in an appropriation statute are to be construed as limited to articles of a like kind with those specifically enumerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canonical rule of statutory construction as applied to appropriation acts (synopsis).
